correctness.rationale: All \(24+576+13824\) four-candidate profiles with one through three labeled voters are exhaustively checked. Two exact formulations agree for Kemeny and two for maximin. The divergent relation, size histogram, eight canonical classes, and orbit sizes are replayed from the embedded verifier.

evidence: Courtin–Mbih–Moyouwou define maximin as the largest minimum pairwise support and Kemeny by maximum pairwise agreement, and their three-candidate analysis proves the relevant score orderings coincide.
Brandt–Dong–Peters place maximin and Kemeny at the same node of their three-candidate correspondence Hasse diagram, explicitly meaning identical outputs for all profiles.
Courtin–Mbih–Moyouwou state that the equivalence no longer holds once there are more than three alternatives.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broader theorems supply the candidate lower bound and the existence of some larger-candidate separation, but they do not imply that two voters still force equality at four candidates or determine the complete three-voter layer.

value.rationale: The result isolates the first point where two canonical but conceptually different Condorcet extensions cease to be interchangeable after their exact three-candidate collapse. The sharp voter threshold, one-sided refinement, exact frequency, and eight symmetry classes make the finding a natural structural benchmark rather than a routine isolated example.
